items.gist: The āṇava procedure is set out for those seeking the supreme abode; when vikalpa's saṃskāra arises, attainment of desired objects, enjoyment, and liberation becomes certain.
For some, vikalpa becomes stable through one's own svātantrya alone; for others it depends on another upāya, as the earlier rule states.
Vikalpa is cinmātra in nature yet functions as niścaya that joins the aṇu to freedom; this niścaya is manifold, and the upāyas differ by near and far.

items.topic: paramārtha in cognitive and embodied levels
items.gist: Even in buddhi, prāṇa, body, and limited knower, paramārtha shines; from pure consciousness, prāṇa and the rest are non-different, giving a double nature of inert and conscious.

items.topic: jīva as Śiva's śakti and non-dual recognition
items.gist: The jīva is Śiva's śakti, present everywhere; when its own nature is realized, one becomes non-dual by concealing the inert aspect, like a face in a mirror.
Pure self-consciousness is ascertained as distinct from buddhi and prāṇa, yet ultimately non-different; through purity, the world-form becomes undivided.

items.topic: no migration and divine power in faculties
items.gist: There is no migration into prāṇa or body; even unseen things are made determinate by vikalpa, and divine power operates directly in buddhi, prāṇa, and body.
Vikalpa does not apply to the void-like knower; buddhi is dhyānamayī, prāṇa is uccāraṇa, and the body is the aggregate of senses and objects.

items.topic: heart meditation on fire, sun, and moon
items.gist: The free consciousness abiding in the heart is meditated as all tattvas; the yogin perceives the heart like a banana bud and meditates the union of soma, sūrya, and agni.
In the great heart-kuṇḍa, the fire of Bhairava blazes; the three powers of fire, sun, and moon are contemplated as mātṛ, māna, and prameya, each threefold as creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
A fourth unbounded form is added, making twelve goddesses like sun-discs; the supreme cakra radiates from the heart through the senses into their respective objects.
The cakra assumes the form of soma, sūrya, and agni in each sense-object; by this graduated yoga, the all-pervading cakra dissolves the layers of the world-path effortlessly.
In the great Bhairavī cakra surrounded by consciousness, the world is destroyed by saṃskāra alone; the yogin meditates the cakra's burning and dissolution until it becomes peaceful.
In that consciousness, the dissolved object shines as consciousness itself; by repeatedly dissolving and re-emitting the world, one constantly attains Bhairava-nature.
The yogin visualizes cakras from triśūla through various numbered forms up to countless thousands, with unwavering attention.
There is no limitation in the great Lord of consciousness; the world is His śaktis, while Maheśvara is the possessor of śakti, as Śrīkaṇṭha taught in the Māṅgalaśāstra.
This dhyāna is the first upāya, taught by Śambhunātha; by the same direction, other dhyānas that lead to the supreme upāya without sequence are also to be adopted.
The prāṇa vṛttis are now explained as an upāya; one meditates void-like non-bliss in the heart, then supreme bliss in the object arising with prāṇa.
Standing in supreme bliss, one reaches samāna and becomes full of brahmānanda; then, resting in udāna-fire, one meditates great bliss.
Without support, great pervasion remains free of vyāna's limitation; cidānanda is not strengthened by inertia, and no division or bhāvanā has real place there.
This is the world-bliss taught by Śambhu; proper rest there is the ultimate state, even though heart and other levels share one nature.
The sixfold form born from prāṇa-uccāra is explained through pervasion; crossing the triśūla region, one resorts to the three nāḍīs and four-petaled lotus.
The wise enter through equality of icchā, jñāna, and kriyā śaktis, ascending the ladder of śaktis from bhrū-bindu to nāda, and rest in visarga like a fish in water.
Entering the heart with expansion and contraction, one rejoices; one resorts to the Bhairava-yāmala rooted in expansion and contraction, in the heart of unified great root and śūla-release.
